title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 117
paragraphs: While Xerxes was at Acanthus, it happened that the man who had been in charge of the making of the channel, Artachaees by name, died of sickness. He was held in high regard by Xerxes, belonged to the Achaemenid family, was in stature the tallest of all the Persians — falling short by only four fingers of being five royal cubits in height — and he had the loudest voice of any man. Xerxes was deeply grieved at the loss of him, and carried him out and buried him with great honor, and the whole army joined in heaping up a mound for him. The people of Acanthus, on the instruction of an oracle, sacrifice to this Artachaees as a hero, invoking his name in their worship.
